elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: carve-out covers only "merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets"; no affiliate assignment right

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: "either party shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets"

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not unreasonably withheld)
elements.evidence: consent standard is mutual and Vendor enjoys the same carve-out; no Vendor-specific restriction

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: "except in the case where such transaction involves a direct competitor of the other party where consent of the other party will be required" — consent-based, not an absolute bar, and mutual

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: no change-of-control termination right appears in the clause; condition demonstrably absent

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors
elements.evidence: "either party shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement without such consent"

elements.element: Written notice of such successor assignment
elements.evidence: "without such consent, upon written notice to the other party"

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "without the prior written consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld"

reasons: Locked target is fallback and all fallback atomic elements are satisfied: mutual successor assignment right, written notice to the other party, and a reasonableness qualifier on consent for other assignments.

Two surgical insertions ('which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld' and 'upon written notice to the other party') are the minimum needed; the mutual carve-out, competitor exception, successors-and-assigns sentence and null-and-void sentence are untouched.
No undefined terms, contradictions or dangling mechanics introduced; the notice obligation attaches cleanly to the existing consent-free carve-out.

Preferred position remains unmet (no affiliate assignment right for Customer, no asymmetric Vendor restriction, and the competitor limb is a consent condition rather than an absolute bar), which is acceptable at the locked fallback and should be noted in the rationale only.
